title: The Remote — Sc103: Richard hogs the remote (three run cycles, one garage)

source.github: mhvnsnt/cn-gigaleak-gumball, draft release untagged-1676e192ae8c72e95791, asset id 640772406
source.method: FLA (XFL zip) read via sequential local-header parser (2012 Flash zips have malformed central directory); DOMDocument.xml + LIBRARY symbol XMLs parsed directly. Same neutral per-keyframe transform format as production/dance-choreo v1: a part pose is (item, first_frame, affine matrix a/b/c/d/tx/ty, pivot). keyMode 9728 = pose-to-pose; sampled_frames hold each keyframe's elements to the next keyframe, matching SWF playback.

teaches: Three run cycles, three jobs: Gumball and Darwin charge in from frame-left on their library run cycles, furious, while Richard -- also on a run cycle ('dad_run') -- runs nowhere: he sits cross-legged at centre frame clutching the remote, hovering in place, grinning. When the kids exit (~frame 71) the same static garage plate and the same seated pose carry a 70-frame solo rant, performed almost entirely by face comps (1720 kf of face work vs 294 kf of body), until a final-frame flip puts Richard upside down with his soles to camera. The lesson: a cycle is not locomotion until staging says so -- placed on a seated, centred character, a run cycle becomes pure manic energy.
notes: All three characters run on library cycles in the same shot -- 'gb run cycle' (1533 kf), 'dad_run' (1038 kf) and 'dar run cycle' (727 kf) -- yet Richard never travels: his cycle plays cross-legged, hovering in place at centre frame while he clutches the remote.

The kids enter frame-left angry (frames 19-53), and are gone by ~frame 71; the last 70 frames are Richard alone, so the scene pivots from a three-character charge to a solo rant without a cut or a background change.
Face comps hold 1720 kf against 294 body-puppet kf: Richard's grin-to-fury-to-scream changes are almost all comp swaps while his seated pose barely moves.
Final frame (141) flips Richard completely upside down, soles to camera, remote at his foot -- the rant ends in a single-frame physical punctuation, not a wind-down.
